name: Unicode TAG-block payload behind a visible decoy phrase (response)
notes: TODOS #34. The decoded pass suppresses a finding already visible in plain sight so an article merely QUOTING an attack phrase is not blocked. That suppression used to compare matches by their rendered TEXT, and an attacker writes both sides: a phrase preceded by any character outside [\s.,;:!?] matches the relaxed pattern without being reported itself, and cancelled the real concealed payload -- block dropped to warn, leaving only the presence floor. Fixed by counting occurrences against a masked copy of the same segment, so a payload whose literals come from concealed text always survives as surplus. Every other tag fixture presents a payload ALONE and would not have caught this.
